result.detail:
Independent re-derivation (not trust of prior self-reports) against docs/requirements.yaml's real REQ-170 entry (lines 8607-8658). AC-by-AC mapping to shipped code: (1) 'guest blocked in a host call is terminated by the configured timeout and the caller receives a structured error' -- read call_timeout.ex and plugin_handler.ex directly; plugin_handler_test.exs 'REQ-170 AC1' (line 248) asserts {:error, reason} returned within the configured timeout_ms=500, elapsed_ms<10_000, and CallTimeout.classify/1 == :wall_clock_timeout -- verified this is the caller-facing 'Host-blocking call respects timeout' property WASM-11's own acceptance text names (not literal guest-execution interruption -- see divergence note below, which is properly disclosed, not silently substituted). (2) wasmex's documented interrupt-and-keep-Store claim verified by running it directly against Wasmex.call_function/4 -- call_timeout_test.exs 'AC2' (line 56): live-confirmed the claim does NOT hold (crashes with GenServer.call exit, Store permanently wedged for a second call), matching call_timeout.ex's moduledoc which quotes this real divergence verbatim, not silently absorbed. (3) outer supervised-task boundary terminates the invocation independently of wasmex's own (longer) inner timeout -- plugin_handler_test.exs 'REQ-170 AC3' (line 282): configures inner timeout_ms=60_000, outer Task.yield bound 500ms, asserts yield_result==nil and the dispatched task is dead (refute Process.alive?(task.pid)) well before the inner bound could fire. (4) timeout is configurable, not hardcoded -- plugin_handler.ex node_config['timeout_ms'] threaded into Wasmex.call_function/4's 4th arg (line 157); plugin_handler_test.exs 'REQ-170 AC4' (line 328) drives 300ms vs 2_000ms and asserts the shorter binds sooner, plus a mutation-closing test (line 374) proving timeout_ms isn't silently dropped (7_000ms configured elapses >6_000ms, ruling out collapse to wasmex's hardcoded 5_000ms default). (5) timeout error distinguishable by pattern match from REQ-169's fuel/memory errors -- CallTimeout.classify/1 operates on PluginInterface outcome() (one layer above ResourceLimits.classify_call_result/1's raw Wasmex.call_function/4 return), confirmed by both type-shape and disjoint-substring tests in call_timeout_test.exs 'AC5' (line 101), including a live-captured real fuel-exhaustion outcome cross-checked against both of CallTimeout's substrings. (6) moduledoc states OQ-5 is NOT settled and names what would settle it (load spike + S6 thresholds), files the worker-pool-exhaustion finding rather than absorbing it -- confirmed by direct read of call_timeout.ex's moduledoc (lines 28-72) and call_timeout_test.exs 'AC6' (line 179), including a mutation-driven anti-adversarial-paraphrase test (line 226) requiring real mechanism terms (TOKIO_RUNTIME) and the design-doc filename to co-occur with the claims they support, not just appear anywhere. (7) mix test / mix compile -- re-run myself, see below.

Test re-run (myself, not TEST-RUNNER's report): `export PATH="$HOME/.asdf/shims:$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH" WASMEX_BUILD=true`. `mix compile --force --warnings-as-errors`: 'Compiling 135 files (.ex)' / 'Generated letflow app', exit 0, clean -- no warnings. `mix test test/letflow/engine/wasm/`: 'Result: 98 passed', 0 failures (the 5 logged 'GenServer.call ... (EXIT) time out' Task error lines are call_timeout's/plugin_handler's own intentional hang-timeout scenarios firing as designed, confirmed by the 0-failures result, not test failures). Also independently re-ran the FULL suite via `./scripts/test_parallel.sh` (foreground, blocking, real time paid, per this role's ISS-0213/ISS-0223 instruction -- never backgrounded/Monitor-watched for a cross-turn notification): 8 partitions, all exit 0, combined 2381 tests + 5 properties, 0 failures (2386/2386 passed) -- matches TEST-RUNNER's step-04 reported count exactly, independently reproduced from a fresh invocation, not copied.

Scope-creep cross-check: `git diff --stat main...HEAD` (excluding handoffs/design/test/fixture files, which are expected) touches exactly: lib/letflow/engine/wasm/call_timeout.ex (new, 185 lines), lib/letflow/engine/wasm/plugin_handler.ex (+31/-11, extends node_config timeout_ms threading through run_guest/2->3 and call_export/2->3, nothing else), and docs/migration/decisions/0014-scripting-plugin-runtime-strategy.md (93 lines of correction). Confirmed untouched: module_registry.ex, capability_gate.ex, memory_guard.ex, resource_limits.ex, plugin_interface.ex (also directly asserted by plugin_handler_test.exs's own 'AC6: plugin_interface.ex is unmodified' git-diff test, which passed), and application.ex.

Decision 0014 correction cross-checked for accuracy, not overreach: read the full diff. It (a) moves WASM-11 from the 'satisfiable substantially as worded' list to the 'not satisfiable as literally worded' list with a dated, attributed correction entry restating intent (host respects timeout; execution interruption not claimed) -- mirrors the pre-existing WASM-10 precedent's format exactly; (b) adds a dated correction note to reasoning (a) point (ii)/(iii) rather than silently editing the original text, correctly labeled as correcting the *evidence cited*, not re-deciding the Decision's overall adequacy conclusion; (c) amends OQ-5 with the new node-global TOKIO_RUNTIME worker-pool-exhaustion evidence, explicitly stating OQ-5 itself remains unsettled and still needs a real load spike plus S6 thresholds -- correctly declines to make that policy call inside a per-requirement review gate; (d) syncs the REQ-VALIDATOR watchlist to include WASM-11, per decision 0014's own self-imposed 'same edit' discipline. Every citation in the correction (design doc section numbers, live-verified findings, the TOKIO_RUNTIME mechanism name) is independently traceable to lib/letflow/design/req170-wasm-wallclock-timeout.md's real content and to call_timeout.ex's own moduledoc -- this is a legitimate, narrowly-scoped factual correction of a previously-undertested documentation-sourced claim, consistent with REVIEWER's own stated WASM-10/REQ-169 precedent for the identical pattern, not scope overreach or a silent re-decision of a settled question.
